summary.name: Perplexity Computer
summary.one_liner: Perplexity Computer is a cloud-based general-purpose AI agent that breaks an described outcome into subtasks, runs sub-agents across multiple AI models, and can execute workflows over hours or months.
keywords: ai agent for research and documents
use_cases: image and video generation within a workflow
long-running tasks lasting hours or months
summary.what_it_does:
Perplexity Computer takes a described outcome, splits it into tasks and subtasks, and creates sub-agents to carry them out, such as web research, document drafting, data processing, or API calls to connected services. It coordinates these automatically and asynchronously, and users can run multiple Computers in parallel. Each task runs in an isolated compute environment with a filesystem, a browser, and tool integrations. The page says it routes work across models: Opus 4.6 as the core reasoning engine, Gemini for deep research, Nano Banana for images, Veo 3.1 for video, Grok for lightweight speed tasks, and ChatGPT 5.2 for long-context recall and wide search. Users can also pick specific models for subtasks.</three_sentence_placeholder>
<parameter name="pricing">paid
notable: Orchestrates multiple frontier models (Opus 4.6, Gemini, Nano Banana, Veo 3.1, Grok, ChatGPT 5.2) and routes subtasks to the one suited for each
Sub-agents run in isolated compute environments with a real filesystem, real browser, and tool integrations
Runs asynchronously for hours or months and can run many instances in parallel
caveats: Available to Perplexity Max subscribers; the page does not give a price, and the listing cites $200/mo
Enterprise Max users get access later; the page says 'soon'
Users must manage token budgets when choosing models, per the page's remarks on token budgets
